title: How Much Does It Cost to Refinish Hardwood Floors in Seattle? (2026 Real Prices)
meta: Seattle hardwood floor refinishing costs $1.99–$6.50 per sq ft in 2026. See Wills Flooring's published rates, a live calculator, and what changes the price.
keywords: hardwood floor refinishing cost Seattle, refinish hardwood floors Seattle WA, cost to refinish wood floors 2026, Seattle floor refinishing price per square foot

blocks.lead: In Seattle, refinishing hardwood floors costs $3.99 per sq ft for a natural finish, $6.50 with stain, and $1.99 for a screen-and-recoat.
blocks.detail: Those are Wills Flooring's published 2026 rates, with a 500 sq ft minimum. A typical 850 sq ft Seattle main floor lands between $3,400 and $5,500.

blocks.html: Search Reddit for "refinish hardwood floors Seattle cost" and you get quotes from $2 to $9 per square foot and a lot of confused homeowners. The spread is real, but it is not random. Almost all of it comes from four things: whether you actually need sanding, whether you want stain, how many stairs you have, and how much furniture is in the way. This post breaks down each one using our published numbers so you can price your own floor before anyone knocks on your door.

items.tag: Floor looks dull but no bare wood
items.title: Screen and recoat
items.text: Light abrasion plus one fresh coat of finish. No dust, one day, and you keep the color you have. Only works if the old finish is intact.

items.title: Sand and refinish, natural
items.text: Full sanding to bare wood, then three coats of Bona water-based finish. Removes scratches, gray boards and pet stains that have not gone deep.

items.title: Sand, stain and finish
items.text: Everything above plus a stain coat and the extra dry time that comes with it. This is how red oak becomes a modern light or espresso floor.

blocks.note: Prices from Wills Flooring's published price list. 500 sq ft minimum. Stairs, dust containment and appliance moves are priced separately below.

blocks.text: Why Seattle quotes range so widely

items.title: Sanding vs recoating
items.text: A recoat is a third of the price of sanding. Many companies only quote full sanding because it pays better. If your finish is dull but not worn through, ask for a recoat first.

items.title: Stain adds $2.51 per sq ft
items.text: Stain is a second full process: the floor is water-popped, stained, dried overnight and then top-coated. Half of the Seattle floors we stain are going lighter, not darker.

items.title: Stairs are priced per tread
items.text: Expect $55 to $75 per tread. A typical Seattle split-level with 13 stairs adds $715 to $975, which explains a lot of the surprise on written quotes.

items.title: Old Seattle houses
items.text: Craftsman and Tudor floors in Ballard, Wallingford and West Seattle are often 90-year-old fir or oak. They sand beautifully but need more patching, and thin fir sometimes limits how many more sandings it can take.

blocks.text: When refinishing is not worth it

a.title: Worth it when
items: Wood is at least 3/32 in above the tongue
Damage is surface scratches, gray finish, light pet stains
You want to keep the character of an original Seattle floor
Budget is under $6 per sq ft

b.title: Skip it when
items: Boards are cupped from a long-term leak
The floor has already been sanded four or more times
You want wide-plank or a species the house never had

blocks.title: One Seattle-specific warning:
blocks.text: Many 1920s to 1950s homes have an old-growth fir floor under carpet. Fir refinishes at the same price as oak but is softer, so a natural finish with no stain and a satin sheen holds up best. We will tell you what you have before we quote.
How to get the lowest real price, not the lowest quote

items.html: Ask whether a recoat is possible. It is the single biggest saving, and it is only an option while the old finish is still intact.
Book in late fall or winter. Seattle refinishing demand peaks from May to September. Off-season scheduling is easier and we can often bundle rooms.
Clear the rooms yourself. Every hour a crew spends moving furniture is an hour not sanding.
Get the square footage in writing. A quote on "about 1,000 sq ft" is not a quote. We measure to the foot and bill the measured area, never the whole house.
Check the warranty. Wills Flooring backs every refinish with a 1-year workmanship warranty, and we are Bona Certified Craftsmen, which matters for the finish itself.

faq.q: How much does it cost to refinish 1,000 sq ft of hardwood floors in Seattle?
faq.a: At Wills Flooring's published rates, 1,000 sq ft costs $3,990 for a natural finish, $6,500 with stain, or $1,990 for a screen-and-recoat. Stairs, dust containment and appliance moves are extra.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to refinish or replace hardwood floors?
faq.a: Refinishing is usually a third to half the cost of new hardwood. New engineered hardwood installed by Wills starts at $3.25 per sq ft for labor plus material, so a refinish at $3.99 all-in is almost always the better value if the boards are sound.

faq.q: How long does refinishing take in Seattle?
faq.a: A natural finish on 800 to 1,000 sq ft takes three to four days including cure time between coats. Stain adds a day. You can walk on the floor in socks after 24 hours and move furniture back after 72.

faq.q: Does the 500 sq ft minimum mean I cannot refinish one small room?
faq.a: You can, but the job is billed at 500 sq ft. For a 300 sq ft bedroom that means $1,995 at the natural rate. Most Seattle customers add a hallway or a second room to use the minimum fully.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to refinish floors in Seattle?
faq.a: No. Refinishing is cosmetic work and needs no City of Seattle permit. Condos often require a building notice and elevator reservation, which we help with.
